runLabel: IMVUSA (blind) - Stage 5/7 - Agent 05 WordPress/Elementor Builder (READ-ONLY PLAN)

output.summary: Build plan decomposing the approved Imvusa site_blueprint, design_system, and content_pack into discrete Elementor implementation tickets. Scope covers Home, Services, Leather Couches, Gallery, Contact Us (George/Bloemfontein), Fabrics & Collections, About, and Get a Quote, plus a canonical Contact Block component and global Elementor design system setup. This is a read-only planning pass: no credentials were used, nothing was executed on any live or staging site, and every ticket remains subject to the full BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL -> QA -> FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT -> CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING -> HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL -> LIVE pipeline. Nothing is WooCommerce-related as this is a lead-generation/consultation business, not ecommerce. All tickets are GREEN or AMBER; none are RED since no payments, shipping, or DNS/registrar actions exist for this business. Two tickets are explicitly flagged AMBER pending human confirmation of real-world facts this pipeline cannot verify on its own: which George phone number and which Bloemfontein address are actually correct.

scope: Elementor Site Settings > Global Colors: color.bg.base, color.bg.surface, color.brand.primary, color.brand.secondary, color.accent.warm, color.cta.primary, color.text.primary, color.text.muted, color.border.subtle, color.feedback.success, color.feedback.error
Elementor Site Settings > Global Fonts: font.display, font.body, font.accent

Base button style for CTA using color.cta.primary

risks: This is a genuinely blind planning pass: no U-Proof, no prior client knowledge, no browsing or image-analysis tool access, and no execution on any live/staging system. Every ticket below is a proposal for human review, not a verified fact.

The George phone number mismatch cannot be resolved by this pipeline — the plan can only route both candidate values into one editable global template; a human/client must confirm which number is actually correct before either the Contact Block or the Fix-George-Phone ticket can be marked complete.
The Bloemfontein address mismatch has the same limitation: this plan cannot determine which address is correct, only that there must be exactly one going forward, pending human confirmation.

design_system v1 explicitly discloses that every color, font, and imagery recommendation is an unverified hypothesis with no access to real site photography, logo, or brand assets — implementing the Global Design System ticket as final without human visual verification would violate the BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL doctrine.

content_pack v1 does not include copy for the blueprint-added About and Get a Quote pages (it explicitly scoped only Home, Services, Leather Couches, Gallery, Contact Us). Building these pages now risks shipping placeholder/lorem content that must not be mistaken for approved copy.

No real photography has been supplied for Leather Couches or Gallery pages; editorial content tickets will need placeholder image slots, and launching with placeholders risks looking unfinished if not tracked as an explicit pre-launch QA item.

Wiring the Get a Quote form to live email/CRM delivery is out of scope for this AMBER planning pass and must go through separate explicit human approval and QA/regression testing before any real lead data flows through it.

Because this run had no tool access, none of the proposed scope, copy mappings, or component structures have been checked against the actual current live Imvusa site; the 'de-duplication' and 'mismatch fix' tickets are based solely on the research_report/blueprint's description of the problem, not a fresh direct observation.

No ecommerce/WooCommerce component exists in this plan per task instruction; if the client's real business model includes any transactional element not disclosed in the supplied artifacts, this plan would need to be revised.

All permission levels assigned here are AMBER or GREEN per doctrine (no RED, no payments/DNS/registrar actions), but every AMBER ticket still requires explicit human approval before any execution — this plan authorizes nothing on its own.
